parameters.description: Award identifier to inspect. Treat this request field as the endpoint's carrier for canonical_award_lookup_id: if you are chaining from v2__search__spending_by_award, pass generated_internal_id unchanged here; if you are chaining from v2__awards__award_id, pass generated_unique_award_id unchanged. Documentation prefers generated natural award ids but also allows deprecated numeric surrogate award ids for backward compatibility. This handoff preserves award identity only; it does not carry any originating search time_period into funding automatically.

documented.notes: Docs describe either a generated natural award id string or a numeric surrogate award id. Generated ids are preferred because they are effectively permanent.

observed.notes: Observed working as a string identifier in a live POST. Reviewer-backed drilldown evidence also confirmed CONT_AWD_HT940216C0001_9700_-NONE-_-NONE- carried successfully from search generated_internal_id into this request body field.

constraints: Treat award_id as the endpoint's request-field carrier for canonical_award_lookup_id.
When chaining from search or award detail workflows, reuse canonical_award_lookup_id unchanged rather than substituting the display Award ID.
Generated award identifiers are preferred over numeric surrogate ids.

Passing canonical_award_lookup_id preserves award identity only; interpret scope from this endpoint's reporting_fiscal_* fields because an upstream spending_by_award time_period is not inherited automatically.

parameters.description: Primary safe pattern for ordering funding records: set sort explicitly whenever row order matters. The documented enum is usable and reviewer-backed safe-template evidence confirmed explicit sort=reporting_fiscal_date works; the contradiction concerns only the service default when sort is omitted.

documented.notes: Docs say object_class sorts by object class code/name, program_activity sorts by code/name, and reporting_fiscal_date sorts by reporting fiscal year/month.

observed.defaultBehavior: With sort omitted, live results were grouped by account_title descending, and within the same account the 2017 row appeared before the 2022 row instead of reporting_fiscal_date descending.
observed.notes: Explicit sort=reporting_fiscal_date with order=desc was reviewer-confirmed in a successful safe-template drilldown call. Set sort explicitly whenever deterministic ordering matters.

constraints: Prefer the safe explicit-sort template whenever pagination order, comparisons, or presentation order matter.
Use one documented sort value when deterministic ordering matters.
Treat omitted sort as unsafe because live/default behavior contradicts the documentation.
The contradiction is about the omitted default behavior, not about explicit documented sort values.

parameters.description: Sort direction for the selected sort key. Pair this with an explicit sort field in the safe request pattern rather than relying on omitted-sort defaults.

constraints: Prefer supplying order together with explicit sort for deterministic pagination and comparisons.

templates.name: basic-award-funding-page
templates.description: Fetch the first funding page for one award using canonical_award_lookup_id under request body field award_id, with a small page size.

templates.name: safe-template-award-funding-page
templates.description: Primary safe template for one page of funding records using canonical_award_lookup_id under request body award_id plus explicit pagination and ordering so callers do not rely on contradicted omitted-sort behavior. This stabilizes order but does not change the accounting-slice grain or inherit any originating spending_by_award time_period, so page 1 cannot be read as the current-period total from an upstream bounded search.

response.shapeSummary: JSON object containing a results array of award funding rows and a page_metadata object; a live probe returned four rows for one award and page_metadata showing no next page for that sample. Rows are labeled by this endpoint's own reporting fiscal period fields, so a bounded time_period from an upstream spending_by_award screen does not carry into funding automatically.

pagination.notes: Pagination uses request-body page and limit controls plus response page_metadata next/previous flags; neither docs nor the retired low-level artifact expose a total result count.

contradictions.statement: When sort is omitted, documentation says the default is reporting_fiscal_date, but the live baseline response was ordered by account_title descending and showed 2017 before 2022 within the same account, contradicting a reporting_fiscal_date descending default.
contradictions.impact: Treat omitted sort as unsafe for deterministic pagination, comparisons, or presentation order. Set both sort and order explicitly; reviewer-backed safe-template usage confirmed explicit reporting_fiscal_date sorting works.

contradictions.statement: Documentation types disaster_emergency_fund_code as boolean, but the live response returned null and the string code 'Q'.
contradictions.impact: Treat this field as a raw code/string-or-null value rather than a boolean until corroborated by DEFC reference material.

quirks.statement: The retired low-level artifact reports that unknown award ids return HTTP 200 with an empty results array rather than an explicit not-found error, but this specific bundle did not re-probe that behavior on 2026-05-10.
quirks.impact: Callers should treat empty results as either a legitimate no-data case or a missing-award case and validate the award id separately when needed.

quirks.statement: The live sample contained null gross_outlay_amount values while still returning valid rows.
quirks.impact: Aggregations should handle null outlay amounts explicitly rather than assuming every row has a numeric outlay value.

gaps.statement: Documentation does not provide total result counts, and the retired low-level artifact also notes there is no total-count pagination metadata.
gaps.impact: Clients must paginate iteratively using hasNext or next instead of precomputing a last page.

gaps.statement: The meaning of any disaster_emergency_fund_code letter values is not explained in the endpoint docs.
gaps.impact: Agents should preserve the raw field and avoid hard-coding business meaning without corroborating DEFC reference material.

risks.statement: Related award-search, award-detail, and award-funding endpoints relabel the same generated award business key: search emits generated_internal_id, award detail echoes generated_unique_award_id, and this endpoint accepts the same value as request field award_id.
risks.impact: Normalize the handoff value as canonical_award_lookup_id and pass it unchanged when chaining across award drilldown endpoints.

risks.statement: Funding rows are period-specific accounting slices rather than deduplicated award totals, and results can be sparse enough to diverge sharply from headline award totals. In the reviewer-backed HT940216C0001 drilldown, award detail reported total_obligation 51269205263.03 while funding returned one 321840 row with hasNext false.
risks.impact: Use this endpoint for funding composition and time-sliced accounting context, not as a single authoritative award total. If you compare to award detail, check whether total_account_obligation is the closer benchmark before expecting reconciliation to total_obligation.

risks.statement: Even with the reviewer-backed safe explicit-sort request pattern, page 1 can be dominated by repeated same-period accounting slices rather than distinct obligation events. In the Sandia drilldown, page 1 returned five FY2026 Q2 month-6 rows with transaction_obligated_amount null and gross_outlay_amount values 4906371.73, 2359010.76, 630711.31, 3398742.41, and 1210.35 while hasNext remained true.
risks.impact: Do not narrate first-page rows as an obligation leaderboard or a full-award total. Treat them as funding/outlay slices for one reporting period and paginate further if broader coverage is needed.

risks.statement: Cross-endpoint award handoff preserves award identity but not search-period scope. In the reviewer-backed Regents drilldown, a bounded v2__search__spending_by_award FY2026 screen (time_period 2025-10-01 through 2026-09-30) handed off canonical_award_lookup_id CONT_AWD_DEAC3243AL00036_8900_-NONE-_-NONE- into funding, yet funding page 1 returned reporting_fiscal_year 2025 rows and page_metadata.hasNext true.
risks.impact: Do not treat page membership or page-1 funding rows as the FY2026 amount that caused the upstream search hit. Re-establish scope from reporting_fiscal_year, reporting_fiscal_quarter, reporting_fiscal_month, and pagination before making current-period claims.

measureInterpretations.name: Funding row order
measureInterpretations.meaning: Funding row order is request-dependent. The safe analytical pattern is to set both sort and order explicitly because the documented omitted-sort default is contradicted by live and reviewer-backed behavior.
measureInterpretations.safeUse: When row order, ranking, pagination review, or page-to-page comparison matters, call the endpoint with an explicit documented sort value plus order and preserve that same ordering pattern as you page.
measureInterpretations.unsafeUse: Do not infer a stable default ranking, chronology, or comparison basis from responses where sort was omitted.
measureInterpretations.dashboardWarning: Before ranking or comparing funding rows, set explicit sort and order; omitted-sort output should be treated as unsafe for deterministic analysis.

measureInterpretations.name: Transaction obligated amount
measureInterpretations.meaning: transaction_obligated_amount is the obligation value for one funding/accounting slice of the requested award, not a deduplicated award total. Valid rows can still have null transaction_obligated_amount when the page is carrying outlay-oriented accounting slices.
measureInterpretations.safeUse: Use this value with reporting period, federal account, object class, program activity, and pagination context to describe slice-level funding activity for the same award.
measureInterpretations.unsafeUse: Do not treat a first page of rows as a complete obligation ledger, a stable leaderboard, or the award's total funding.
measureInterpretations.dashboardWarning: Safe explicit sorting can still return repeated same-period rows with null transaction_obligated_amount and hasNext true, so keep paging before turning page-1 rows into award-level summaries.

measureInterpretations.name: Gross outlay amount
measureInterpretations.meaning: gross_outlay_amount is also reported at the funding-slice grain. It can be populated on valid rows even when transaction_obligated_amount is null, so it reflects accounting/outlay context rather than a single award-total measure.
measureInterpretations.safeUse: Use gross outlay values to describe period-specific outlay slices within the returned reporting-period and classification grain.
measureInterpretations.unsafeUse: Do not read a few outlay rows as the full current-period spend for the award or as a direct substitute for award-detail headline totals.
measureInterpretations.dashboardWarning: Repeated same-period outlay slices on page 1 are accounting context, not a full-award subtotal; paginate further and reconcile carefully before aggregating.

measureInterpretations.name: Reporting fiscal period scope
measureInterpretations.meaning: reporting_fiscal_year and its companion quarter/month fields define the funding row's own reporting-period scope. These rows can follow a bounded spending_by_award handoff for the same award without inheriting that search time_period automatically.
measureInterpretations.safeUse: When you arrive from a bounded spending_by_award screen, carry canonical_award_lookup_id unchanged, then read reporting_fiscal_year, reporting_fiscal_quarter, reporting_fiscal_month, and page_metadata before saying anything about current-period funding.
measureInterpretations.unsafeUse: Do not assume that because an award appeared in an FY2026 search screen, page-1 funding rows or funding page membership automatically represent FY2026 spend or the amount that caused inclusion in that search.
measureInterpretations.dashboardWarning: Award identity carries across endpoints, but time scope does not: funding rows must be interpreted by their own reporting-period fields and page 1 is not a current-period total.

recommendedFollowups.trigger: You arrived from a bounded v2__search__spending_by_award screen and want to make a current-period funding claim for the same award.
recommendedFollowups.reason: Carry canonical_award_lookup_id unchanged, but re-establish scope using reporting_fiscal_year/reporting_fiscal_quarter/reporting_fiscal_month and paginate as needed; the originating search time_period is not inherited automatically.

recommendedFollowups.trigger: page_metadata.hasNext is true, or the first page is dominated by repeated same-period funding slices.
recommendedFollowups.reason: Continue paging with the same award_id and the safe explicit sort/order pattern before claiming complete coverage, stable rankings, or a full-award summary.

recommendedFollowups.trigger: Funding rows look sparse or much smaller than an award-detail headline obligation figure.
recommendedFollowups.reason: Re-check the same award in award detail and compare against total_account_obligation before expecting funding rows to reconcile to total_obligation.
